state: Chat transcript, HomeNet support, 2026-09-21 21:14. CUSTOMER: Every night after about 8pm the internet crawls. Netflix buffers, my Zoom call with my sister in Lisbon froze three times tonight and she thought I'd hung up on her. Daytime it's fine, I work from the kitchen table on the laptop most mornings with no trouble at all. My laptop and my phone both do it at night. AGENT: Sorry to hear that. Could you run a speed test on a device plugged into the router with a cable? CUSTOMER: My son's gaming PC is wired, he says his speed is fine at night, he's playing right now with no lag, he'd be yelling if there was lag, believe me. I just ran the test on the laptop over wifi in the living room, 4 Mbps down, 2 up. Last week a friend told me to switch to the 5GHz one but I don't know what that means, there are two names that show up, HomeNet-4471 and HomeNet-4471-5G, and I've always used the first one because it shows more bars. AGENT: Thanks. I see no outages or congestion alerts for your node (HN-221) tonight, and your plan is 500 Mbps. Your router reports 23 other wifi networks visible on the same 2.4GHz channel as yours. CUSTOMER: Yeah we're in an apartment block, loads of networks, the building has something like 60 flats and everyone got new routers when the landlord put in the new cabling last year. Is that bad? Do I need someone to come out? I'm home Saturday morning if so. I also want to know if I can get a discount this month because I've basically not had internet in the evenings for two weeks, and I pay for 500 which I'm clearly not getting. The router is in the hall cupboard next to the electrics, the installer put it there, and the living room is at the other end of the flat. AGENT: Let's try a couple of things first, and I'll note the credit request. CUSTOMER: ok but I've already restarted the router like 5 times this week and my neighbour on another provider says his is fine, so I don't really get why it's us. Honestly if this carries on I'll look at switching, but I'd rather not, the price is good.

request.text: Hi, we added my daughter's line to our Family Unlimited plan two weeks ago with the free Galaxion A35 promo. It turns out her school gives students a free phone and plan, so we'd like to remove her line and send the phone back. She hasn't really used it, it's been in the box on her desk apart from setting it up. Also, while I'm here, can we drop the whole account from Family Unlimited ($160) to Family Essentials ($110)? We're trying to cut costs because my husband's hours were reduced. The other three lines have been on the account for years and none of us use much data, maybe 5 GB each. I don't want to lose anything important, but $50 a month is a lot for us right now. If it's easier to do by phone let me know, but I'd rather do it here.

ticket.text: Since last Monday staff inside the clinic get no signal in the surgery and x-ray rooms. The front desk is fine, and the car park is fine. We rely on mobiles for on-call vets: when a vet is in surgery the on-call phone is left on the counter in the prep room next door, and if it doesn't ring we miss emergency calls from farms. We've tried restarting phones, turning off Wi-Fi calling and back on, and our IT guy moved the Wi-Fi access point closer to the surgery. Nothing has changed in the building except the new lead-lined x-ray room was finished two weeks ago, which is right between the prep room and the rest of the building. We just need this fixed, we don't care how. If it means buying something, we'd need a quote for the partners to approve first.

email_thread.subject: Cancel - moving abroad
email_thread.body: Hello, I'm relocating to Italy permanently on October 15 for a new job. Please cancel my mobile line (555-0139) and home internet effective that date. I'm under contract until next June on the internet. I understand there may be a fee but I'm leaving the country so I can't use the service anyway. I've attached my Italian employment contract and my one-way flight booking. I'll also need to know how to return the router and the TV box; I won't have a car after the 10th, so a courier pickup would be ideal. Could you also confirm that my final bill will go to my personal email, since my work email will be closed?

Hi Lucia, I've scheduled the cancellation of both services for October 15. Please note the early termination fee of $180 applies to the home internet agreement. The mobile line is month-to-month, so no fee. For equipment, you can drop it at any store or use a prepaid return box; courier pickup isn't available in your area. Your final bill will go to the email on file.
I thought there was an exception for moving abroad? A friend said she didn't pay anything when she moved to Canada. Can you check? Also, which email is on file? I want to be sure it's this one.

You're right to ask. Our terms include a relocation exception. I've sent this to the retentions team to review your documents. On the email question, I've updated the account email to this address as you asked. A prepaid return box will be posted to you this week.

state.personal_statement: When I was twelve, my younger brother was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes. I watched my mother learn to count carbohydrates, calculate insulin doses and wake every three hours at night to check his levels. I started keeping a notebook of his readings and noticed that his numbers spiked on days he had PE at school. When I showed this to his nurse, she adjusted his morning dose on PE days. That was the first time I realised that paying close attention to data could change someone's day. Since then I have volunteered at a diabetes youth camp for three summers, where I help the nurses log the campers' readings and run a quiz evening about food labels, and I completed an online course in human physiology. At school I chose biology, chemistry and mathematics, and for my extended project I compared the carbohydrate labelling of twenty common snacks with laboratory values published by the national food agency, finding that four of them understated sugar content by more than ten percent. I want to study nutrition because I have seen how much everyday decisions about food matter for people living with a chronic condition, and I want to learn how to give families better tools than a paper notebook.

matches.source: Applicant's sibling's application to the same university, 2024 (internal database)
matches.overlap: 61% of the first paragraph - near-identical wording about a younger brother with type 1 diabetes, notebook of readings, PE-day spikes, and the nurse adjusting the dose

integrity_policy.IP-1: Substantial overlap (over 25% of the whole document) with another application is referred to the Integrity Panel.
integrity_policy.IP-2: Siblings may describe shared family experiences; overlap in facts is not itself a breach, but reuse of another person's wording is.
integrity_policy.IP-3: Reviewers must not make a finding; the Integrity Panel decides.
integrity_policy.IP-4: Where overlap is with a sibling's application, the panel may invite the applicant to explain before deciding.
